October 10 — William Chapman, 24, visits Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster alone. Witnesses see him pacing with his headphones in and dancing near the tigers, asking strangers to take his photo with the tiger behind him. At about 1:30 p.m. he climbs over two fences from the raised walkway into the Land of the Tiger enclosure. A woman tries to pull him back. He approaches Altai, a five-year-old Amur tiger. Rangers fire warning shots, the tiger retreats to a shelter and is secured, and Chapman is pronounced dead at the scene. The park is evacuated and closed. October 10 — South Yorkshire Police ask the public not to share the distressing footage circulating online. The park confirms Altai will not be euthanised and is safe and well. October 13 — Chapman is identified by his stepfather. He was a former child actor — Alfie Chaplin in ITV's "May Contain Nuts" (2009) and the young Edward Jenner in BBC Learning's "True Stories" (2012) — and a self-employed online trader. His family releases a statement: he had suffered significant mental illness for several years, the circulation of offensive media content is causing them severe distress, and they ask people to stop sharing it. President Trump posts the attack clip to Truth Social, drawing condemnation. October 15 — The inquest opens at Doncaster Coroner's Court before Senior Coroner Nicola Mundy. The hearing is told Chapman had a diagnosis of schizophrenia and previous psychosis, was under Doncaster adult mental health services but assessed as highly functioning and independent, and that his family raised concerns about his contact with those services. The Rotherham, Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust launches its own investigation; City of Doncaster Council runs a health and safety investigation to be shared with the coroner. Provisional cause of death: multiple traumatic injuries / animal interaction. The inquest is adjourned. October 16 — Yorkshire Wildlife Park reopens, including Land of the Tiger, with specialist trauma support for staff. Current status — Inquest adjourned to March 18, 2027. NHS trust and council investigations ongoing. Altai remains at the park, safe and well. #YorkshireWildlifePark #Doncaster #Altai #Tiger #uknewsheadlines

A man climbed into a tiger enclosure at a wildlife park in England. Moments later, the tiger attacked him — and he never made it out alive. The incident happened on October 10, 2026, at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster, England. Authorities have identified the victim as William Chapman, a man in his early 20s who was visiting the park alone. According to South Yorkshire Police, emergency services were called shortly after 1:30 p.m. after reports that a man had entered the tiger enclosure. Inside was a five-year-old Siberian tiger named Altai. Witnesses described seeing the man approach the animal while other visitors shouted warnings. Reports say some people tried to get him to stay away from the tiger. But he entered the enclosure. The tiger attacked, leaving the man with fatal injuries. Emergency responders rushed to the scene, but he was pronounced dead at the park. Video of the incident has since circulated online. Authorities have urged people not to share the distressing footage out of respect for the victim and his family. Investigators are still examining the circumstances surrounding the incident. And there's another detail people have been asking about: what happened to the tiger? The wildlife park confirmed that Altai was unharmed and **will not be euthanized**. The park was temporarily closed following the incident while authorities carried out their investigation. This is a tragic reminder that even animals raised in managed environments remain powerful wild predators. A barrier separating visitors from an animal is there for a reason, and entering an enclosure can have irreversible consequences. William Chapman’s family is now grieving his death, and officials are asking the public to respect their privacy. What do you think should happen when a visitor deliberately enters a dangerous animal's enclosure? Should the animal ever be held responsible for reacting instinctively? #antdolla #hoodtalez #scarystories

Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.
